name: 2R spherical shoulder + C-ring axial bearing on the upper arm
verdict: dead: gap 129.98 vs 68.93 for the spherical 3R on the same bench (25 configurations); not worth a GPU sweep - the limiter is structural: the C-track's carriage must travel ~220 deg round the arm (axial rotation turns p2's azimuth 1:1) but a circular track about any GH-through humerus-fixed axis hugs the arm only over its lateral +-60 deg
note: best = sweep entry 8; Bench(60,160) fast grid cache, kit conventions (march, K2 dense, K6 + by-construction track/carriage/slide), audit clean; branch sigma -1 essential (sigma +1: links 0 in band); red team: rest taken 2.7 mm, overhead contact hub1 -6.0 mm, abd75+ext90 / int90 jam (carriage outside C), across-body taken 5.5 mm, behind-back taken 1.3 mm; pinches link2 0.26 mm, track 0.31 mm; cam-track variant indicative only (track in-band 0.88, contact in most poses); baseline 3R 68.93
limiter: axial travel vs circular track: required track radius (median / p90 pose) 49/57 mm for a +-60 deg span vs 73/87 mm for the +-110 deg the carriage needs (L=100); best (cov 0.6, R 57) loses 75/89 lost ws poses and 11/16 lost clip frames to 'carriage outside the C' (abduction 75 with +-90 axial rotation jams), track in-band14 0.13, carriage 0.00; full C (cov 0.95) R 86.5, contact 0.80. Overhead (plane 30 elev 150): hub 1 6 mm inside the skin. Spec fix: the GH-elbow line runs 3-8 mm under the skin at mid-arm and exits overhead, so the track axis is tilted 18 deg

audit.reason: reproduced 129.98 exactly on Bench(60,160); no modelling bug or convention mismatch found; full-travel C needs R 94.7 mm and gives contact 0.85 (gap 325) - circular track cannot both cover the axial travel and hug the arm
